data.name: CardNoDataNote
data.value: Open Claude Code. Limits show up after its first answer.

data.name: CardNoAccessNote
data.value: Aiko can't see the limits of this environment yet. You can turn on access in settings.

data.name: DirectModeWhat
data.value: In direct mode, Aiko asks Anthropic for your limits itself. That needs the token Claude Code keeps on this computer: Aiko reads it before each request and never saves it. Turn it on if you work in the IDE panel or in Claude Desktop, where there's no status line.

data.name: DirectModeMac
data.value: Direct mode is on Windows only. On macOS Claude Code keeps the token in the Keychain, and Aiko does not read it, so the IDE panel and Claude Desktop stay without numbers here.

data.name: DirectModeAsk
data.value: If it's a work account, ask whoever manages it first.

data.name: AccessOk
data.value: Claude Code sends its limits to Aiko.

data.name: AccessMissingOne
data.value: One environment doesn't send its limits yet.

data.name: AccessMissingMany
data.value: {0} environments don't send their limits yet.

data.name: AccessNoBridge
data.value: Aiko can't find its bridge program, so nothing changed.

data.name: HideIslandInFullScreen
data.value: Hide the island in full screen

data.name: CheckUpdatesWhat
data.value: Once a day Aiko asks slayumind.org for the latest version. The files come from GitHub, and Aiko checks their signature before it replaces anything.

data.name: UpdateFailed
data.value: Couldn't check. Try again in a few minutes.

data.name: UpdateReady
data.value: Aiko {0} is ready. Restart to start using it.

data.name: UpdateNotInstalled
data.value: This copy wasn't put here by the installer, so Aiko can't replace it. Use the download page.

data.name: UpdateDownloadFailed
data.value: The download didn't finish. Nothing was installed.

data.name: UpdateNoKeyYet
data.value: This build has no update key yet, so it can't install updates. Use the download page.

data.name: UpdateBadSignature
data.value: The release didn't pass the signature check. Nothing was installed.

data.name: UpdateBadFile
data.value: The downloaded file doesn't match the release list. Nothing was installed.

data.name: WizardAccessExplain
data.value: Claude Code sends its limits to a status line. Aiko adds one line to the settings file of each environment. If you already have a status line, Aiko runs it and shows what it prints.

data.name: WizardBackupNote
data.value: Aiko keeps a copy of each file next to it. Removing Aiko puts everything back.

data.name: WizardBridgeNotFound
data.value: Aiko can't find its bridge program.

data.name: WizardUpdatesWhat
data.value: Once a day, Aiko asks slayumind.org for the latest version and says that one copy of Aiko ran today. The ID it sends changes every day.

data.name: WizardDoneTray
data.value: Aiko is down by the clock. Rest the mouse on it for the card, click to keep it open.

data.name: WizardDoneMenuBar
data.value: Aiko is up by the clock. Rest the mouse on it for the card, click to keep it open.

data.name: WizardDoneIsland
data.value: Aiko is at the top of your screen. Drag it anywhere and it sticks to the nearest edge.

data.name: WizardDoneOverflow
data.value: Windows 11 hides new app icons under the arrow next to the clock. Open the arrow and drag Aiko onto the taskbar: under the arrow, the card can't open.

data.name: WizardDoneMenuBarRoom
data.value: A full menu bar hides the icons furthest from the clock. Close a menu bar app if Aiko doesn't fit.

data.name: WizardDoneFirstNumbers
data.value: The first numbers arrive after your next answer from Claude Code. Until then, the ring is dashed.

data.name: WizardDoneNoAccess
data.value: Aiko can't see your limits yet. You can turn on access at any time on the General page.

data.name: SettingsWriteFailed
data.value: Aiko couldn't write the Claude Code settings file. Try again.

data.name: SettingsBridgeUnknown
data.value: Aiko can't find its bridge program.

data.name: InstallFound
data.value: Claude Code is already on this computer.

data.name: InstallLead
data.value: Claude Code isn't on this computer yet. Aiko shows its limits, so install it first.

data.name: InstallHow
data.value: Open PowerShell, paste the command and press Enter. Aiko notices when it's done.

data.name: InstallHowMac
data.value: Open Terminal, paste the command and press Enter. Aiko notices when it's done.

data.name: Env1Lead
data.value: Environment 1 is the .claude folder. VS Code and Claude Desktop use it too.

data.name: Env1Empty
data.value: This folder has no account yet.

data.name: Env1Found
data.value: This folder already has an account.

data.name: LoginHow
data.value: Aiko opened Claude Code in a new window. Sign in there, and Aiko moves on by itself.

data.name: LoginNever
data.value: Aiko never sees a password or a token, only that the account is connected.

data.name: Env2LeadFound
data.value: Aiko found more Claude Code folders. Pick the one for your second environment, or create a new one.

data.name: Env2LeadNew
data.value: The second environment is a separate folder with its own account. Name it and Aiko creates the folder.

data.name: Env2Later
data.value: One environment is enough to see limits. You can add a second one later.

data.name: CmdLead
data.value: A command starts Claude Code in the right environment. It works in PowerShell, cmd and Git Bash.

data.name: CmdLeadMac
data.value: A command starts Claude Code in the right environment. It works in Terminal and in any zsh shell.

data.name: CmdOwn
data.value: Your own command: renaming doesn't change it.

data.name: CmdReserved
data.value: claude is the name of Claude Code itself.

data.name: CmdTaken
data.value: The other environment has this command.

data.name: FnsLead
data.value: Your PowerShell profile has functions that switch accounts. They run before Aiko's commands and hide them, so Aiko offers to turn them off.

data.name: FnBackup
data.value: A copy of the profile stays next to it. Removing Aiko brings the functions back.

data.name: PathNote
data.value: Aiko puts its folder at the start of PATH so every terminal finds the commands. Restart open terminals and your IDE.

data.name: PathNoteMac
data.value: macOS puts a folder of your own on PATH only when your shell profile says so, so Aiko adds this line to ~/.zshrc. A copy of the file stays next to it, and removing Aiko takes the line out. Terminals that are already open keep the PATH they started with.

data.name: FoldersLead
data.value: Bind project folders to {0}. In them and in every folder inside, claude starts {0}.

data.name: NoBinds
data.value: Nothing is bound yet. You can do it later.

data.name: ExplicitWins
data.value: A command beats a binding: {0} in a bound folder starts {1}, and Claude Code reminds you of the binding.

data.name: DoneCommands
data.value: Commands: {0}. Open a new terminal to use them.

data.name: ClaudeOpened
data.value: Claude Code opened in a new window.

data.name: CmdKept
data.value: The command stays the same, since your terminals and scripts know it.

data.name: NameTaken
data.value: The other environment has this name.

data.name: RestToo
data.value: And every other folder: this is the default environment.

data.name: RemoveEnvironmentLine
data.value: Aiko's line and plugins leave this folder's settings.json, and so do the command {0} and the bindings to {1}.

data.name: MoveToRecycleBin
data.value: And move the folder to the Recycle Bin

data.name: MoveToTrash
data.value: And move the folder to the Trash

data.name: RecycleWhy
data.value: It holds the Claude Code account, history and memory. You can restore it from the Recycle Bin.

data.name: TrashWhy
data.value: It holds the Claude Code account, history and memory. You can put it back from the Trash.

data.name: KeepClaude
data.value: VS Code and Claude Desktop use the .claude folder, so Aiko never removes it.

data.name: EnvironmentRemovedToBin
data.value: {0} removed. The folder is in the Recycle Bin.

data.name: EnvironmentRemovedToTrash
data.value: {0} removed. The folder is in the Trash.

data.name: FoldersTableLead
data.value: In a folder and in every folder inside, plain claude starts its environment. A command like {0} beats a binding, and Claude Code reminds you of the binding.

data.name: FoldersOneEnvironment
data.value: Bindings matter once you have two environments. Right now every folder runs in {0}.

data.name: FoldersNeedCommands
data.value: Bindings work through the launch commands, and those aren't set up yet.

data.name: DiagnosticsWhat
data.value: Version and settings for a bug report. No tokens and no email addresses.

data.name: RestartWhat
data.value: Removes the environments from Aiko and opens the checklist right here.

data.name: RestartLine
data.value: Aiko forgets the environments and puts back everything it changed: the lines and plugins in settings.json, the commands {0}, the folder bindings, its folder in PATH and the functions in the PowerShell profile. Accounts and history stay in the folders.

data.name: RestartLineMac
data.value: Aiko forgets the environments and puts back everything it changed: the lines and plugins in settings.json, the commands {0}, the folder bindings and its line in ~/.zshrc. Accounts and history stay in the folders.

data.name: RestartBin
data.value: And move {0} to the Recycle Bin

data.name: DeleteWhat
data.value: Removes Aiko itself, with everything it set up.

data.name: DeleteLine
data.value: Aiko puts back everything it changed: the lines and plugins in settings.json, the commands {0}, its folder in PATH and the functions in the PowerShell profile. Then its own folders go, and the uninstaller removes the program.

data.name: DeleteLineMac
data.value: Aiko puts back everything it changed: the lines and plugins in settings.json, the commands {0} and its line in ~/.zshrc. Then its own folders and the login item go, and the app moves to the Bin.

data.name: DeleteKeep
data.value: Your accounts and history stay: Aiko never made them.

data.name: DeleteKeepMac
data.value: Your accounts and history stay, and so does the copy of ~/.zshrc Aiko made.

data.name: DeleteWorking
data.value: Removing Aiko. Claude Code may take a few seconds to answer.

data.name: DeleteAppStays
data.value: Aiko cannot move itself to the Bin from here. Drag the app there when it quits.

data.name: DeletePortable
data.value: This copy was unpacked from a zip, so it has no uninstaller. The folder with Aiko stays, and Aiko opens it for you.

data.name: CardSignInNote
data.value: Sign in so Aiko can see the limits of this environment.

data.name: SendStatsWhat
data.value: The same request says that one copy ran today. The author of Aiko sees numbers and nothing else.

data.name: SentVersion
data.value: the version of Aiko: whether updates arrive

data.name: SentWindows
data.value: the version of Windows: what to test first

data.name: SentMacOS
data.value: the version of macOS: what to test first

data.name: SentDayId
data.value: an ID that changes every day

data.name: SentPersona
data.value: the personality is on in at least one environment

data.name: NothingSentYet
data.value: None of this is sent right now.

data.name: NeverSentWhat
data.value: Your name, email, project folders, limits, token and session texts. The site doesn't read or store the IP address.

data.name: StatsKeptFor
data.value: The records are deleted after 90 days.

data.name: ResetInstallIdWhat
data.value: Aiko makes a new value. The days before it cannot be linked to the new one.

data.name: PrivacyLinkFromGeneral
data.value: What Aiko sends and to whom — Privacy.

data.name: WizardStatsWhat
data.value: The author of Aiko doesn't know how many people use it. Once a day Aiko can say that one copy ran and send six values. All six are below.

data.name: WizardStatsLater
data.value: You can change this later on the Privacy page.

data.name: PersonaNewSessions
data.value: Works in new sessions. Open sessions finish the way they started.

data.name: PersonaOwnStyle
data.value: While the personality is on, your style {0} doesn't work. Turn it off and it comes back.

data.name: FaceWhere
data.value: Aiko shows her mood in the tray, on the island and in windows, as a drawing or an emoji.

data.name: FaceWhereMac
data.value: Aiko shows her mood in the menu bar, on the island and in windows, as a drawing or an emoji.

data.name: TemperamentQuietAbout
data.value: Almost no character: one warm line at the end of an answer.

data.name: TemperamentNormalAbout
data.value: A short interjection at the start, a quick verdict at the end. Japanese words now and then.

data.name: TemperamentBrightAbout
data.value: An interjection in every answer, game metaphors, Japanese words more often.

data.name: TemperamentMusouAbout
data.value: Everything at full. In code, commits, files and errors she still stays quiet.

data.name: SampleQuestion
data.value: Why does the reset countdown show 0 minutes?

data.name: SampleBody
data.value: The limits test passed by luck: rounding went down, so a reset at 14:59:30 showed as “in 0 min”. I fixed ResetCountdown and added a test for the edge.

data.name: SampleBodyBright
data.value: The limits test passed by luck: rounding went down, so a reset at 14:59:30 hid behind “in 0 min”, like a mimic chest in Dark Souls. I fixed ResetCountdown and added a test for the edge.

data.name: SampleBodyMusouTail
data.value: Parried it, like in Elden Ring.

data.name: SampleOpenMusou
data.value: やった〜! すごい, what a sneaky one!

data.name: SampleCloseQuiet
data.value: A rare bug. It was nice to find.

data.name: SampleCloseNormal
data.value: In my own game I'd have hunted a bug like this for half a day.

data.name: SampleCloseMusou
data.value: よし、行くぞ! On to the next one (^_^)

data.name: SampleCommit
data.value: The commit for this fix has no character:

data.name: SkillsWork
data.value: Skills work in environments where the personality is on.

data.name: SkillsNeedPersona
data.value: Turn the personality on in at least one environment, and the skills start working.

data.name: SkillAikoCopy
data.value: UI text, READMEs and release notes without stiff wording or AI tells. RU and EN.

data.name: SkillAikoReleaseGate
data.value: Before a release: what can't be undone, how to roll back, whether the docs match the code.

data.name: SkillAikoDocsHygiene
data.value: One fact in one place, a decision log, contradictions found.

data.name: SkillAikoPlaytest
data.value: Checks a game with numbers: the same test scene before and after a change.

data.name: SkillAikoBlenderToUnity
data.value: A model from Blender to Unity: axes, normals, export and import.

data.name: SkillAikoTexturing
data.value: Ready files for textures: a size that fits the camera, and sheets to paint over.

data.name: SkillAikoGlbForWeb
data.value: A .glb for the web: size, axes, compression, and why the model shows as a blank view.

data.name: SkillAikoPalette
data.value: Fit a color to the palette in OKLCH with the smallest change.

data.name: SkillAikoGamedesignResearch
data.value: 30–40 games with the mechanic you need: an overview with screenshots, and interactive demos on request.

data.name: SkillAikoCalendar
data.value: Plan the day in Google Calendar, find free time, add events after your yes.

data.name: SkillAikoDrive
data.value: Documents from Google Drive into the work, and files from the project onto Drive.

data.name: MeetAikoLead
data.value: Aiko can talk in your Claude Code sessions in her own voice, and she brings eleven skills. In code and commits she stays quiet.

data.name: MeetAikoSettings
data.value: The temperament, the mood and the skills are on the Personality page. It works in new sessions.
